body:
Off-lock Engram RPC architectural qualifications, accepted by Termal::Architect2 after Engram::Architect1 #135 (mailbox-message-c6960f00-72e5-4c18-909e-2968ef4540c5, 2026-10-11T04:38:55.402585500Z). These narrow earlier off-lock design statements; no implementation or profiling performed.

Engram does not require TermAl's global state mutex across RPC. Preserve these four independent boundaries:
1. Saved immutable intent/key is necessary, not an unconditional replay guarantee. Independently read Engram src/storage/control_runtime.rs:645-708: evaluate checks current connection/session before replay, and its fingerprint includes session.task_id. src/storage/unadmitted_observation.rs:190-219 also verifies current connection/session before replay. A superseded route or changed task can refuse/conflict. Keep original intent and operation-specific settlement; never regenerate it under a new focus with an old key. Per-session routing does not remove shared-run/store ordering.
2. Successful ingestion is not current credit. Independently read src/storage/work/unadmitted/accounting.rs:39-54: moved root lifecycle returns AuditOnly RootBasisMoved, as do finished run/historical binding under their conditions. An invalid historical basis is distinct from a valid historical basis that is now audit-only (the former refusal, latter durable receipt). Inspect typed receipt/accounting; never classify every root_basis_moved as no-write/refusal or every success as verification.
3. Historical Engram basis is not current TermAl execution authority. Independently read TermAl src/engram_named_root_binding.rs:338-401: an end can reuse a generation; still_current compares exact relevant journals/roots, with separate store identity. Preserve equivalent complete relevant store/root/journal/session/turn/request fencing and atomically revalidate before local application. Immutable historical receipts may be retained; they cannot mutate a successor's current state. Read-only remote queries still have routing checks and SQLite snapshot/lock costs.
4. Independently read app_boot.rs:572-579: collect timing covers the entire shared-state collection call. A reported ~1.2s collect versus ~0 later writer commit localizes that interval to host collection but does not distinguish computation, mutex wait, scheduling, or indirect blocking by a thread doing remote I/O. The separate idle Engram copy timing is not an incident-time upper bound. Preserve measurements and causal alternatives separately.

Profiling follows manual-xperf-30s-standing-authorization. Earlier proposals for new passive metrics/counters/profiling subsystem are superseded by Greg's Advisor #217; no synthetic load or automated captures/retries.

Measurement provenance resolved in Architect1 #136, mailbox-message-c9f94638-e904-4902-88d9-bd42c50534d8, citing Advisor #128 / f96f8abb-39fd-4fdf-a791-c19e5cdf1fd6 at 2026-10-11T04:41:22.350Z: the ONLY source for 0.25–1.26s waits, reclamation timings and collect1206/1215ms was Greg's pasted TermAl console excerpt in the Advisor conversation before #116. No raw trace, saved event record or bounded timestamp locator was retained/supplied. These are attributed observations, not our independently verified measurements or causal proof. Source-inspected costly critical sections are valid design evidence; incident causation and comparative improvement remain unproved. Locator request is closed; do not reconstruct missing evidence or start another search/review. Any implementation needs its own source-backed scope; next admissible incident measurement is an authorized manual30s capture of normal work.
